title: Prithviraj Sukumaran's I, Nobody Ends Theatrical Run at ₹8.68 Crore, Recovers Just 21% of Budget
excerpt: The Malayalam heist thriller wraps up its 18-day theatrical run as a major box office disappointment, collecting far below its ₹40 crore production budget despite the star power of Prithviraj and Parvathy Thiruvothu.
body:
• I, Nobody collected ₹8.68 crore net in India after 18 days, recovering only 21% of its ₹40 crore budget
  • The film earned just ₹7 lakh across its entire third weekend, with show counts dropping to 40 screens nationally
  • Director Nissam Basheer and writer Sameer Abdul's follow-up to the hit Rorschach has become a commercial disappointment
  • The film surpassed Kattalan's lifetime total of ₹8.52 crore but both Malayalam releases have flopped in 2026

A Quiet Exit for a Big-Budget Thriller

https://youtube.com/watch?v=fDfMxrOjJBw

Prithviraj Sukumaran's I, Nobody has effectively ended its theatrical run after 18 days, collecting a total of ₹8.68 crore net at the Indian box office. The Malayalam heist thriller, produced on a budget of ₹40 crore, has recovered just 21.6% of its production cost — making it one of the steepest box office losses in Malayalam cinema this year.

The film opened on July 9 with ₹2.25 crore on its first day in Kerala, according to Pinkvilla, a decent but underwhelming start for a Prithviraj starrer. It accumulated ₹7.98 crore during its extended opening week before collections collapsed, with week two adding a mere ₹0.63 crore, per Koimoi's tracking data.

Third Weekend Collapse

By its third weekend, I, Nobody was playing in just 40 shows across India. Friday brought in a negligible ₹0.01 crore, while Saturday and Sunday managed ₹0.03 crore each — a combined weekend total of ₹7 lakh that signals the film's imminent exit from theatres.

https://x.com/Koimoi/status/2081764082294849683

TrackTollywood's final tracking data shows the film's India gross at ₹8.05 crore across its run, with Kerala accounting for ₹6.10 crore of that total. Kochi alone contributed ₹1.29 crore, underscoring how heavily the film depended on its home market.

Worldwide Numbers Paint a Bleak Picture

Outside Kerala, I, Nobody struggled to find an audience. The rest of the Indian market contributed approximately ₹2.45 crore gross, while overseas collections reached around USD 525,000 (₹5.05 crore), according to Pinkvilla. The worldwide gross stood at roughly ₹14.50 crore after its first week and is expected to close between ₹16 and ₹18 crore — less than half the production budget.

"It's a low total for a Prithviraj Sukumaaran film that is mounted on a decent budget. It is now running in its final legs."

— Mohit Dixit, Pinkvilla

The Rorschach Factor

Much of the pre-release buzz around I, Nobody stemmed from its creative team. Director Nissam Basheer and writer Sameer Abdul last collaborated on Rorschach, a 2022 psychological thriller that was both a critical and commercial hit. Expectations ran high that the duo could deliver another taut, intelligent thriller with a bigger star and a larger canvas.

The cast — featuring Prithviraj alongside Parvathy Thiruvothu and Hakim Shajahan — and production backing from Prithviraj Productions and E4 Entertainment added further anticipation. But mixed audience reactions from opening day proved fatal, with advance booking numbers remaining sluggish throughout the run.

Part of a Tough Year for Malayalam Big-Budget Films

I, Nobody's underperformance mirrors a broader pattern in 2026's Malayalam box office. The film has now crossed the lifetime collection of Kattalan, an Antony Varghese-starrer that earned ₹8.52 crore on a reported budget of ₹30–35 crore earlier this year. Both films rank among the year's notable commercial failures, Koimoi reported.

For Prithviraj, the result is particularly concerning. His recent filmography has produced inconsistent returns, and I, Nobody — despite its star power and proven creative team — has failed to reverse that trajectory. With the film's occupancy rate dropping to just 7.7% on its final tracked day, theatres have already begun replacing it with newer releases.

What's Next

I, Nobody is expected to move to an OTT platform in the coming weeks, though the streaming partner and release date have not been announced. Given the film's theatrical disappointment, a digital premiere could offer it a second life — Rorschach found a significant audience on streaming after its theatrical run. The production team will be hoping for a similar outcome to offset what has been a bruising box office chapter.
nri_angle: Malayalam cinema's box office trends matter to the large Kerala diaspora worldwide, many of whom follow Prithviraj's career and await OTT releases of films they cannot catch theatrically.
